independent.summary: Every created workspace gets a fresh full AI allowance: `Workspace.create` sets no `aiBudget`, so the schema default `grantedMicros = AI_TRIAL_GRANT_MICROS` ($3.50) applies and `usageMeter.js` meters per workspaceId. Before this change only `POST /auth/register` (IP-capped by KOL-050/081) could mint a grant; now any logged-in user can mint up to `WORKSPACE_MAX_PER_OWNER` (10) of them with cheap `template: null` creates — ~10x the intended paid-provider spend per account. The cap's rationale in the route and the Decision Log weighs only the DB cost of a seed, and neither the route nor `createWorkspace()` zeroes or shares the grant.

The test titled 'sends nothing without a name, and nothing twice' only exercises the empty-name case and the disabled button; it never submits twice, so the `workspaceCreating` double-submit guard in `createNewWorkspace` is unasserted despite the title claiming it.

triageGrades.reason: The diff edits `POST /auth/register` and adds a session-only, `requireAuth`-gated create route that writes an owner membership, so auth is squarely touched.
The only `.env.example` additions are a numeric cap (`WORKSPACE_MAX_PER_OWNER`) and a log level; no credential, token or key handling is touched anywhere in the diff.

Each create writes a `Workspace` carrying a micro-dollar AI allowance (the new test even asserts a forged `aiBudget` is ignored), so the change does touch the spending-allowance surface — see independent finding 1.
The diff rewrites registration's rollback block that does `User.deleteOne(...)` (adding a log line to it), so irreversible-delete code is in the change.
No outbound calls are added — templates and seeding are local code and MongoDB only.
No version bump, migration or deploy config change; the new env var has an in-code default so no release step is required.

summary: The local model reported nothing at all, so it produced no false positives but also missed both real issues — notably that each new workspace mints a fresh AI spending allowance — and two of its six triage answers (secrets, money) are wrong.
